title: Reproduce the CHSH optimum with an exact certificate
statement: For a bipartite quantum state and local Hermitian observables A0,A1,B0,B1 with eigenvalues in {-1,+1}, reproduce the universal bound |<A0 tensor B0>+<A0 tensor B1>+<A1 tensor B0>-<A1 tensor B1>| <= 2 sqrt(2), including an attaining realization and an exact upper-bound certificate.
status_basis: The inspected source supplies a proof and attaining certificate. The project proposes a reproduction task, not a new bound.
plain_summary: Rebuild a standard limit on quantum correlations in a form another person can check exactly. This calibrates statement translation and certificate checking before unfamiliar Bell problems are considered.
assumptions: A normalized positive quantum state on a tensor-product bipartite Hilbert space.
Each of two local observables per party is Hermitian and squares to identity; the operators act on their own tensor factors.
Expectations use the same state and the displayed sign convention; this task adopts the tensor-product formulation.
scope: Universal bound under the stated quantum model; a finite-dimensional attaining example; exact 4 by 4 Gram-matrix certificate. No experimental analysis.
target: A reproducible derivation and independently checkable exact upper- and lower-bound certificates for an already known result.
success_criteria: Define the CHSH expression and all normalization conventions explicitly.
Provide an exact feasible Gram matrix and dual witness with matching objective values, or a complete independently checked operator proof plus an attaining construction.
Explain why the certificate concerns every allowed state and observable, not only sampled numerical examples.
Record any discrepancy between source notation, generated mathematics and checking code.
known_results: Wehner Section 2 proves the optimum 2 sqrt(2) by semidefinite duality; Section 3 extends the method to a family of chained inequalities.
The result is a known theorem, so reproduction success has no mathematical novelty.
prerequisites: Tensor products, density operators and Hermitian matrices.
Positive semidefinite matrices, Gram matrices and weak duality.
Exact arithmetic over Q(sqrt(2)) or an equivalent symbolic representation.
significance: Useful as a compact calibration of proof-certificate discipline and normalization handling. Its scientific value here is workflow reliability, not a new quantum bound.

relations.explanation: Both use exact Gram constraints, but MUB existence is a different and much harder problem; calibration success supplies no evidence that it is easy.

requirements.experiment: None for the mathematical reproduction. Physical realization and loophole analysis would be separate experimental tasks.
requirements.data: No empirical dataset; use the cited mathematical definitions.
requirements.compute: A few fixed 4 by 4 exact matrices. A standard local symbolic or rational-algebra environment is a plausible resource class; no runtime or monetary estimate has been measured.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Quantum tensor-product model and dichotomic projective observables as stated. A broader measurement or operator-algebra model requires a new alignment check.

ai_assessment.rationale: A fixed operator-proof calibration with an attaining construction is a useful priority trial. If the alternative SDP route is chosen, first resolve the documented source transcription hazards and normalization alignment. No trial results have been recorded.

ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes tool-using AI with literature retrieval, exact algebra or rational linear algebra, code generation, and access to a human domain reviewer.

obstacles: Losing a factor of two when translating the quadratic objective.
Confusing a numerical lower bound with a universal upper bound.
Using the wrong tensor ordering or silently changing allowed observables.
A source itself can contain a typographical inconsistency; independent algebra remains necessary.

steps: Freeze the precise statement and tensor ordering.
Derive the Gram objective and dual using one normalization throughout.
Check diagonal constraints and positive semidefiniteness exactly, with a second checking path where possible.
Check matching objectives and a valid quantum realization.
Have a reviewer compare the certificate theorem with the original physical assumptions.
Justify extension from the source pure-state representation to every density operator in the declared scope, or use a direct operator argument that covers the full state class.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Moderate: a linear-algebra reviewer can inspect certificates, but a quantum-information reviewer should confirm statement alignment.
validation.statement_alignment: A valid SDP calculation proves the original bound only after the representation theorem or direct operator reduction is justified; a finite realization demonstrates attainability.

known_attempts: Published proof: Stephanie Wehner (2006), Section 2. This is a literature record, not an AI attempt or a project experiment.
